text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Service redwood-v2-small (streaming) p99 latency crossed 2.2s at 07:15 UTC — SLO breach triggered. Affected route: /chat/stream. Auto-created incident channel. Link: https://internal.alerts/INC-1719004321
oncall-alex: ack. I'm taking first responder. Paging SRE now.
sre-maya: joining. can someone paste p95/p99 and the time window? Any deploys or config changes in the last 30m?
eng-jonathan: we pushed a quantization bake and auto-apply for redwood-v2-small at 07:10 UTC (commit: git/infra@f3b2a). Profile applied: int8+fp8 hybrid with KV-cache compression enabled. Deploy command: `./infra/deploy --model redwood-v2-small --profile quant-bake-2024-06-xx`
ml-infra-ian: confirmed: `quant-bake` job ran at 07:09:42. It flagged higher-than-expected activation outliers in layers 8-10 causing KV cache thrash. Sample metric: 
```
window=5m p50=120ms p95=340ms p99=2250ms error_rate=0.6% stream-stalls=0.9%
kv-evict-rate=180/s (baseline 30/s)
```
support-lucy: noticing 7 support tickets in last 20m, 3 mention partial streaming (clients saw truncated tokens then reconnect). CS flagged one enterprise customer (acme-inc) experiencing user-reported stalls.
product-gabi: is this isolated to redwood-v2-small or other sizes? any routing fallbacks?
ml-infra-ian: appears isolated to the quantized variant. FP16 baseline (redwood-v2-small-fp16) p99 stable ~380ms. The auto-apply process flipped traffic to the new profile; some connections hit high tail due to KV cache eviction + dequant overhead on long-context streaming.
sre-maya: mitigation options: 1) route streaming traffic to fp16 variant, 2) disable kv-cache compression on quant profile, 3) temporarily reduce batching/concurrency for that pool. Which is fastest?
eng-jonathan: I'm executing a traffic shift to the fp16 variant now: `router promote --from redwood-v2-small:quant-bake-2024-06 --to redwood-v2-small:fp16 --percent 100 --immediate`
ops-bot: Router change submitted by eng-jonathan. Change ID: rchg-202406-171900. Requesting approval... auto-approved for incidents.
ops-bot: Traffic rebalancer: 100% of streaming requests for model redwood-v2-small now routed to redwood-v2-small:fp16 (applied in 12s).
ml-infra-ian: disabling auto-apply for future quant bakes for this family: `infra quant-config set --family redwood-v2-small --auto-apply false`. Recommending to run isolated calibration offline and validate KV eviction patterns.
sre-maya: monitoring... current metrics after route change: 
```
window=5m p50=110ms p95=360ms p99=420ms stream-stalls=0.15%
kv-evict-rate=28/s
```
eng-jonathan: rolling back the quant profile auto-apply flag and queueing a regression: created ticket INFRA-4982 to bake with stricter eviction thresholds and add simulated long-stream tests.
support-lucy: informing ACME account team: we pushed traffic to fp16 and are investigating; will open a priority ticket and offer mitigation credits if needed.
product-gabi: please capture timeline and signal we can share with customer. Also need postmortem; assign owner?
oncall-alex: i'll own the incident postmortem. Action items: 1) eng to complete regression bake (INFRA-4982), 2) ml-infra to add eviction checks to bake pipeline, 3) SRE to run synthetic long-stream smoke, 4) Support to contact impacted customers.
oncall-sam: (evening oncall) taking over in 30m. summary for handoff: p99 spikes on quantized redwood-v2-small after quant-bake auto-apply; root cause appears to be KV-cache thrash + dequant overhead under long streaming contexts; immediate mitigation was routing to fp16. Current status: stable, p99 ~420ms. See rchg-202406-171900 and INFRA-4982.
sre-maya: adding retrospective notes: add a canary stage for quant-bakes that runs stateful streaming workloads for 10k+ tokens to detect tail regressions.
oncall-alex: thanks team. tagging: @oncall-sam for handoff, @ml-infra-ian for the regression, @eng-jonathan for router change, @support-lucy for customer comms. Closing active paging. :white_check_mark:
